Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our ops team dug into projected sustained loads for Q3 and we want to validate two things with Redwood before we sign the Dedicated contract:

1) Admission curve behavior for sustained-heavy workloads (60k tokens/sec sustained, 5% 99th tail spikes to 120k tokens/sec). We need to know the headroom required per 8xA100-equivalent shard to keep p99 < 350ms for short prompt responses.

2) Network topology implications for our VPC: we plan an egress mesh across three AZs with cross-AZ trunking limited to 10Gbps per link. Is there a recommended egress shaping and tenant admission policy you can commit to as part of the MOP?

I've attached a simple demand table and a rough traffic matrix (privpool_admission_model_v3.xlsx). Colin from our data center vendor is on the thread to validate NIC oversubscription assumptions.

Can we get a short note of recommended baseline provisioning and a proposed MOP timeline by EOD Wednesday? We need this for our internal procurement window.

Thanks,

Sara Nielsen
Head of Platform Operations, NorthBridge.ai

Sara — thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet. I pulled in Laura, Irene, and Jonas since they'll own sizing, networking, and simulations. Quick read: we can give an operational baseline and a staged MOP, but we need to align on a couple of assumptions (queueing policy, KV cache hit-rate expectations, and workload mix).

High level answer up front: for a sustained 60k tokens/sec with 5% spikes to 120k, target committed capacity should start at 1.6x steady (so ~96k tokens/sec committed) with burst headroom enabled via warm standby and cross-AZ burst pools. That keeps p99 headroom under our 350ms target in our tests, assuming a realistic prefix-cache hit-rate (>30%) and continuous batching.

I'll let Irene call out the network/egress constraints and Jonas attach simulation outputs. After that we'll propose a timeline and a short Mutual Action Plan doc.

Sara / team — technical notes on the egress mesh and admission policy (I'll keep it concise):

- Cross-AZ trunking: with 10Gbps per link we must avoid synchronous KV replication or large checkpoint traffic during peak windows. We recommend segregating background replication onto a scheduled maintenance tunnel (off-peak) and dedicating the 10Gbps links to inference traffic.

- Egress shaping: apply per-tenant token-rate policing at the edge (L3) with hierarchical token buckets. If you configure tenant-level burst buckets to allow 2.5x nominal for 120s windows, you can absorb brief spikes without degrading other tenants.

- Admission policy heuristic: accept requests up to committed capacity (1.6x steady in Markus's guidance). Beyond that, route to: 1) warm-standby burst pool (if enabled), 2) queued-with-guaranteed-degradation (drop non-critical requests after 45s queue time), 3) fallback to hosted model (only if agreed in SLA).

- NIC oversubscription: Colin, your vendor spec is fine if per-host oversubscription <= 1.5x and top-of-rack is non-blocking; otherwise prefer 25Gbps NICs to avoid head-of-line queueing.

I attached the network drawing we discussed (egress_mesh_diagram_v2.png) and a short checklist for ops.

Irene Choi
Principal Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attaching the simulation summary and the admission-curves CSV output. Key findings:

- Baseline sim (KV hit 32%, batching distribution typical for chat workload): 96k committed tokens/sec across the cluster yields p99 ~ 310ms and p50 ~ 58ms.
- With KV hit drop to 15% p99 rises to ~420ms at 96k committed; to maintain p99 < 350ms you'd need 1.9x committed (approx 114k tokens/sec).
- Cross-AZ burst routing adds ~12-18ms median latency if trunking saturates; recommend headroom at the AZ egress layer to keep tail impact below 20ms.

I've uploaded the raw CSV and a short README; see the Mutual Action Plan draft for staged commitments.

Jonas Weber
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Sara — summary and action items (final):

1) Provisioning recommendation (initial commit): 1.6x steady-state (96k tokens/sec committed) with a staged evaluation to move to 1.9x if KV hit-rate < 25% during the first 30 days.
2) Network & egress: reserve non-blocking spines and prefer 25Gbps NICs per host; schedule background replication on an off-peak maintenance tunnel. Configure per-tenant hierarchical token buckets with 2.5x short-window burst allowance.
3) Admission policy & fallbacks: warm-standby burst pool + queued-degrade policy + optional fallback to hosted models (requires separate SLA line).
4) Timeline / Mutual Action Plan: we drafted a 3-week rollout plan (attached: mutual_action_plan_NorthBridge.docx). Week 1: baseline provisioning + networking QA; Week 2: controlled canary (20% traffic); Week 3: full cutover and 30-day observation window.

Next steps for NorthBridge ops: confirm PO network uplink (10Gbps vs 25Gbps per host) and approve the staged MOP. Redwood will: upload final sim artifacts, produce a one-page runbook for on-call, and stand up a 72-hour observability window during the cutover.

If that aligns, I'll schedule the kickoff with our solutions team for Monday.

Thanks — Markus
VP, Production Engineering
